messages:
mira: Heads up — saw a ~18% tail-latency regression on Mixtral canary for chat-streaming. Linking the profiler dump below.

jake: can you paste the perf trace? was it kv cache related?

mira: pasted. The flame shows the attention KV step falling back to generic GEMM on A100 for certain sequence lengths. Kernel selector picked 'matmul_generic' instead of 'optimized_kv_v2' when token_count%16 != 0. Profiler snippet:
```
# nvprof summary
kernel optimized_kv_v2: 72 ms
kernel matmul_generic: 211 ms
warning: selector -> generic for seq=503, heads=16
```

li: interesting — seq=503 is odd. Is tokenizer producing extra BOS/EOS tokens? we've seen RoPE scaling triggers around >512 vs 512 boundary

mira: yes, tokenizer produced 503 because of byte-fallback on some non-ascii prompts. Byte fallback caused extra special tokens for emojis and ZWJ sequences. That pushed many requests off the ideal packing boundaries and tripped our batching heuristic. Short bursts (1-4 requests) suddenly had seq variance 100-600.

anya: @mira do you have the batching logs? did the router switch to latency-first mode or something?

mira: router stayed cost-first. But the local batcher turned off continuous batching because batch_size * avg_seq > batcher_max_tokens threshold for some customers. So we ended up with micro-batches and more kernel launches. Logs:
```
batcher: avg_seq=312, var=98, max_tokens=2048 -> disable_continuous_batching
kernel_selector: seq=503 -> choose matmul_generic
```

jake: so root cause chain: tokenizer byte-fallback -> higher token counts -> batching turns off -> fallback kernel chosen -> latency regression. Any quick mitigations?

li: a few options:
- normalize tokenizer: pre-normalize certain unicode sequences to reduce byte-fallback
- treat BOS/EOS trimming for chat templates where possible
- expand kernel selector to include a fallback optimized kernel for odd seq lengths
- tweak batcher threshold to prefer continuous batching with higher token caps

mira: tried a quick patch to pad sequences to multiples of 8 for Mixtral and Llama models; that reduced generic GEMM usage but increased token cost by ~2.3%. Still improved p99 latency by 12% on canary.

anya: what's the impact on cost? customers might care if token counts go up.

mira: measured: unit token cost up slightly but total infra cost down because fewer kernel calls and better utilization. I have numbers in the perf-bot report.

perf-bot: auto-report: canary id=canary-2025-11-04 | p50 -3%, p95 -8%, p99 -12% | infra cost -4% | token count +2.3% | note: mixtral & qwen show similar improvement with pad=8

jake: Qwen too? Qwen had different head/kv dims, no?

mira: Qwen's kv dims are 128 not 64; its kernel selector is more sensitive — but padding helped since the custom kernel has alignment=32 constraints. For Qwen pad=16 was best.

li: long term we should: a) add tokenizer-aware packing (coerce chat templates to minimal special tokens), b) teach kernel selector to consider padded sequences and prefer aligned kernels, c) add a micro-optimized kernel for odd-length small batches.

anya: can someone open a ticket with action items (patch, kernel, tokenizer tweak) and link RFC for batching heuristics? I'll own coordinating with runtime and tokenizer.

mira: creating ticket now, will add perf dumps & example prompts that trigger byte-fallback.

jake: thanks — also let's add a unit test for chat templates that asserts token counts stable across emoji inputs.

li: will add to tokenizer tests. Also we should record RoPE scaling note: when seq crosses the model RoPE base (e.g., 512->2048) the attention kernel uses different rot freq handling which affects kernel perf — include that in docs.

mira: noted. final: short-term mitigation = pad-to-8 for mixtral/llama, pad-to-16 for qwen; medium-term = kernel selector improvement + tokenizer normalization.

anya: :thumbsup:
